name: Cramp-ring

card.summary: A medieval ring amulet, worn as a charm against cramps and seizures and as a personal adornment.

quick.overview:
Cramp-rings were rings said to cure cramps and epilepsy, distributed by English monarchs. They functioned as a charm worn on the finger.

For appearance, they are a historical piece of jewellery; their stated purpose was health protection.
quick.how: The ring is worn on the finger as an amulet.
quick.risks: No risks documented beyond ordinary jewellery.

lead: Cramp-rings were rings that English monarchs distributed, said to cure sicknesses such as cramps and epilepsy.[1] They were worn as jewellery and charms.
No clinical research on them was found.

angle.text: A finger ring worn as an amulet against cramps and seizures.

paras: English monarchs distributed cramp-rings, which were said to be a cure for cramps and epilepsy.[1]
